3: /**
4:  * check-interaction-contract.js — every button of the same class must have
5:  * EXACTLY the same hover, focus-visible and active look.
6:  *
7:  * PART 1 (static): no button state rule (:hover/:focus/:focus-visible/:active)
8:  * may live anywhere except the shared vendor stylesheets (CANONICAL_CSS), and
9:  * no page may use an alias button class that carries its own state rule.
10:  *
11:  * PART 2 (dynamic, headless Chromium): render every PAGES entry, measure the
12:  * hover / focus-visible / active computed-style signature of every button in
13:  * GROUPS/ALIASES and fail if a group has more than one distinct look per state.
14:  *
15:  * Exit 0 only if everything passes; 1 on any violation (each printed as a
16:  * line starting with `FAIL:`). Final line on pass: `OK: ...`.
17:  *
18:  * Also usable as a library: module.exports = { checkInteractionContract }
19:  * where checkInteractionContract is async and returns { ok, failures }.
20:  */
21: 
22: const fs = require('fs');
23: const path = require('path');
24: 
25: const ROOT = path.resolve(__dirname, '..');
26: 
27: const GROUPS = {
28:   secondary: ['button--secondary'],
29:   primary: ['button-checkout', 'button--primary'],
30:   tertiary: ['button-tertiary'],
31: };
32: const ALIASES = {
33:   'product-card-cta-secondary-alt': 'secondary',
34:   'product-card-cta-primary-alt': 'primary',
35:   'product-card-cta-tertiary-alt': 'tertiary',
36: };
37: const PAGES = [
38:   'ongoing_project/MTD/variant-a/index.html',
39:   'ongoing_project/MTD/variant-b/index.html',
40:   'ongoing_project/MTD/mtd-income-tax/index.html',
41:   'ongoing_project/MTD/page/index.html',
42:   'ongoing_project/MTD/page/index-modal.html',
43: ];
44: const CANONICAL_CSS = [
45:   'ongoing_project/MTD/mtd-income-tax/main.css',
46:   'ongoing_project/MTD/page/main.css',
47: ];
48: const STYLE_ROOTS = ['ongoing_project/MTD', 'components'];
49: const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(['.work', 'Assets', 'node_modules', '.git']);
50: 
51: const STATE_PSEUDO = [':hover', ':focus-visible', ':focus-within', ':focus', ':active'];
52: const BUTTON_CLASSES = new Set([
53:   ...Object.values(GROUPS).flat(),
54:   ...Object.keys(ALIASES),
55:   'score-button',
56: ]);
57: const PROPS = [
58:   'backgroundColor', 'color', 'borderTopColor', 'borderTopWidth',
59:   'boxShadow', 'outlineStyle', 'outlineColor', 'outlineWidth', 'textDecorationLine',
60: ];
61: const PROPS_AFTER = [...PROPS, 'transform', 'opacity'];
62: const STATES = ['hover', 'focus', 'active'];
63: 
64: // ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
65: 
66: function rel(p) {
67:   return path.relative(ROOT, p).split(path.sep).join('/');
68: }
69: 
70: function walk(dir, out) {
71:   let entries;
72:   try {
73:     entries = fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true });
74:   } catch {
75:     return out;
76:   }
77:   for (const e of entries) {
78:     if (e.isDirectory()) {
79:       if (SKIP_DIRS.has(e.name)) continue;
80:       walk(path.join(dir, e.name), out);
81:     } else if (e.isFile()) {
82:       out.push(path.join(dir, e.name));
83:     }
84:   }
85:   return out;
86: }
87: 
88: function stripComments(css) {
89:   return css.replace(/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//g, '');
90: }
91: 
92: /** Yield { selector, body } for every style rule, recursing into
93:  *  @media/@supports/@container/@layer and ignoring @keyframes/@font-face. */
94: function* iterRules(css) {
95:   let i = 0;
96:   const n = css.length;
97:   while (i < n) {
98:     while (i < n && /\s/.test(css[i])) i++;
99:     if (i >= n) break;
100:     if (css[i] === '}') { i++; continue; }
101:     if (css[i] === '@') {
102:       const brace = css.indexOf('{', i);
103:       const semi = css.indexOf(';', i);
104:       if (semi !== -1 && (brace === -1 || semi < brace)) { i = semi + 1; continue; }
105:       if (brace === -1) break;
106:       const name = (css.slice(i, brace).match(/^@\s*([\w-]+)/) || [, ''])[1].toLowerCase();
107:       let depth = 0;
108:       let k = brace;
109:       for (; k < n; k++) {
110:         if (css[k] === '{') depth++;
111:         else if (css[k] === '}' && --depth === 0) break;
112:       }
113:       if (name === 'media' || name === 'supports' || name === 'container' || name === 'layer') {
114:         yield* iterRules(css.slice(brace + 1, k));
115:       }
116:       i = k + 1;
117:       continue;
118:     }
119:     const brace = css.indexOf('{', i);
120:     if (brace === -1) break;
121:     const selector = css.slice(i, brace).trim();
122:     let depth = 0;
123:     let k = brace;
124:     for (; k < n; k++) {
125:       if (css[k] === '{') depth++;
126:       else if (css[k] === '}' && --depth === 0) break;
127:     }
128:     if (selector) yield { selector, body: css.slice(brace + 1, k) };
129:     i = k + 1;
130:   }
131: }

133: /** Split a selector list on top-level commas (not inside parentheses). */
134: function splitSelectors(sel) {
135:   const out = [];
136:   let depth = 0;
137:   let cur = '';
138:   for (const ch of sel) {
139:     if (ch === '(') depth++;
140:     else if (ch === ')') depth--;
141:     if (ch === ',' && depth === 0) {
142:       if (cur.trim()) out.push(cur.trim());
143:       cur = '';
144:     } else cur += ch;
145:   }
146:   if (cur.trim()) out.push(cur.trim());
147:   return out;
148: }

150: function classTokensOfSelector(sel) {
151:   const names = [];
152:   const re = /\.([A-Za-z_][\w-]*)/g;
153:   let m;
154:   while ((m = re.exec(sel))) names.push(m[1]);
155:   return names;
156: }
157: 
158: function hasStatePseudo(sel) {
159:   return STATE_PSEUDO.some((p) => sel.includes(p));
160: }
161: 
162: function isButtonStateSelector(sel) {
163:   if (!hasStatePseudo(sel)) return false;
164:   return classTokensOfSelector(sel).some((t) => BUTTON_CLASSES.has(t));
165: }
166: 
167: /** All class-attribute values of one html file. */
168: function classAttrsOf(html) {
169:   const out = [];
170:   const re = /class\s*=\s*("([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')/g;
171:   let m;
172:   while ((m = re.exec(html))) out.push(m[2] !== undefined ? m[2] : m[3]);
173:   return out;
174: }
175: 
176: function classWordIn(attrs, word) {
177:   return attrs.some((a) => a.split(/\s+/).includes(word));
178: }
179: 
180: function groupOfClassList(classList) {
181:   for (const c of classList) {
182:     if (ALIASES[c]) return ALIASES[c];
183:   }
184:   for (const c of classList) {
185:     for (const [g, names] of Object.entries(GROUPS)) {
186:       if (names.includes(c)) return g;
187:     }
188:   }
189:   return null;
190: }
191: 
192: // ---------------------------------------------------------------- PART 1
193: 
194: function staticChecks() {
195:   const failures = [];
196:   const fail = (msg) => { failures.push(msg); console.log('FAIL: ' + msg); };
197: 
198:   const files = [];
199:   for (const root of STYLE_ROOTS) walk(path.join(ROOT, root), files);
200: 
201:   const canonical = new Set(CANONICAL_CSS.map((p) => path.join(ROOT, p)));
202: 
203:   // alias usage in PAGES (needed for the canonical-file rule)
204:   const aliasUsedInPage = new Map(); // alias -> page rel
205:   for (const page of PAGES) {
206:     const abs = path.join(ROOT, page);
207:     let html = '';
208:     try { html = fs.readFileSync(abs, 'utf8'); } catch { continue; }
209:     const attrs = classAttrsOf(html);
210:     for (const alias of Object.keys(ALIASES)) {
211:       if (!aliasUsedInPage.has(alias) && classWordIn(attrs, alias)) {
212:         aliasUsedInPage.set(alias, page);
213:       }
214:     }
215:   }
216: 
217:   for (const [alias, page] of aliasUsedInPage) {
218:     fail(`${page}: uses alias button class ${alias}; use the shared class ${GROUPS[ALIASES[alias]][0]} instead`);
219:   }
220: 
221:   for (const file of files) {
222:     const ext = path.extname(file).toLowerCase();
223:     let sources = []; // { label, text, isCanonical }
224:     if (ext === '.css') {
225:       let text = '';
226:       try { text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'); } catch { continue; }
227:       sources.push({ label: rel(file), text, isCanonical: canonical.has(file) });
228:     } else if (ext === '.html') {
229:       let html = '';
230:       try { html = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'); } catch { continue; }
231:       const re = /<style\b[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/style>/gi;
232:       let m;
233:       while ((m = re.exec(html))) {
234:         sources.push({ label: rel(file), text: m[1], isCanonical: false });
235:       }
236:     } else continue;
237: 
238:     for (const src of sources) {
239:       const css = stripComments(src.text);
240:       for (const rule of iterRules(css)) {
241:         for (const sel of splitSelectors(rule.selector)) {
242:           if (!isButtonStateSelector(sel)) continue;
243:           if (!src.isCanonical) {
244:             fail(`${src.label}: button state selector outside the shared definition: ${sel}`);
245:             continue;
246:           }
247:           for (const token of classTokensOfSelector(sel)) {
248:             if (ALIASES[token] && aliasUsedInPage.has(token)) {
249:               fail(`${src.label}: alias button class ${token} has its own state rule (second definition of ${ALIASES[token]}): ${sel}`);
250:               break;
251:             }
252:           }
253:         }
254:       }
255:     }
256:   }
257:   return failures;
258: }
259: 
260: // ---------------------------------------------------------------- PART 2
261: 
262: const MIME = {
263:   '.html': 'text/html; charset=utf-8',
264:   '.css': 'text/css; charset=utf-8',
265:   '.js': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8',
266:   '.mjs': 'text/javascript; charset=utf-8',
267:   '.json': 'application/json; charset=utf-8',
268:   '.svg': 'image/svg+xml',
269:   '.png': 'image/png',
270:   '.jpg': 'image/jpeg',
271:   '.jpeg': 'image/jpeg',
272:   '.gif': 'image/gif',
273:   '.webp': 'image/webp',
274:   '.ico': 'image/x-icon',
275:   '.woff': 'font/woff',
276:   '.woff2': 'font/woff2',
277:   '.ttf': 'font/ttf',
278:   '.map': 'application/json',
279:   '.txt': 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
280: };
281: 
282: function startServer() {
283:   const http = require('http');
284:   const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
285:     try {
286:       let urlPath = decodeURIComponent((req.url || '/').split('?')[0]);
287:       if (urlPath.endsWith('/')) urlPath += 'index.html';
288:       const abs = path.resolve(ROOT, '.' + path.posix.normalize(urlPath));
289:       if (abs !== ROOT && !abs.startsWith(ROOT + path.sep)) {
290:         res.writeHead(403);
291:         res.end();
292:         return;
293:       }
294:       const data = fs.readFileSync(abs);
295:       res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': MIME[path.extname(abs).toLowerCase()] || 'application/octet-stream' });
296:       res.end(data);
297:     } catch {
298:       res.writeHead(404);
299:       res.end();
300:     }
301:   });
302:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
303:     server.once('error', reject);
304:     server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => resolve(server));
305:   });
306: }
307: 
308: async function dynamicChecks(failures) {
309:   const fail = (msg) => { failures.push(msg); console.log('FAIL: ' + msg); };
310: 
311:   let chromium;
312:   try {
313:     ({ chromium } = require('playwright'));
314:   } catch {
315:     fail('playwright not installed (npm i -D playwright && npx playwright install chromium)');
316:     return { buttons: 0, pages: PAGES.length };
317:   }
318: 
319:   const server = await startServer();
320:   const port = server.address().port;
321:   const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });
322:   const measurements = []; // { page, group, state -> sig, classAttr, text }
323:   let totalButtons = 0;
324: 
325:   try {
326:     for (const pagePath of PAGES) {
327:       const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } });
328:       try {
329:         await page.route(
330:           (u) => /^https?:/.test(u.toString()) && u.hostname !== '127.0.0.1',
331:           (r) => r.abort()
332:         );
333:         await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/${pagePath}`, { waitUntil: 'load' }).catch(() => {});
334:         await page.evaluate(() => {
335:           document.getElementById('sage-page-gate-lock')?.remove();
336:           document.getElementById('sage-page-gate')?.setAttribute('hidden', '');
337:           document.addEventListener('click', (e) => e.preventDefault(), true);
338:         });
339:         await page.waitForTimeout(600);
340: 
341:         const allClasses = [...Object.values(GROUPS).flat(), ...Object.keys(ALIASES)];
342:         await page.evaluate((classes) => {
343:           window.__ic = [...document.querySelectorAll('a, button')].filter((el) =>
344:             classes.some((c) => el.classList.contains(c))
345:           );
346:         }, allClasses);
347:         const count = await page.evaluate(() => window.__ic.length);
348: 
349:         for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
350:           const el = (await page.evaluateHandle((i) => window.__ic[i], i)).asElement();
351:           if (!el) continue;
352:           await el.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded({ timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {});
353: 
354:           const visible = await el.evaluate((e) => {
355:             const r = e.getBoundingClientRect();
356:             const cs = getComputedStyle(e);
357:             return r.width > 0 && r.height > 0 && cs.visibility !== 'hidden' && cs.display !== 'none';
358:           });
359:           if (!visible) { await el.dispose(); continue; }
360: 
361:           const hitTestable = await el.evaluate((e) => {
362:             const r = e.getBoundingClientRect();
363:             const hit = document.elementFromPoint(r.x + r.width / 2, r.y + r.height / 2);
364:             return !!hit && (hit === e || e.contains(hit));
365:           });
366:           if (!hitTestable) { await el.dispose(); continue; }
367: 
368:           const meta = await el.evaluate((e) => ({
369:             classAttr: (e.getAttribute('class') || '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(),
370:             text: (e.textContent || '').trim().slice(0, 24),
371:             classes: [...e.classList],
372:           }));
373:           const group = groupOfClassList(meta.classes);
374:           if (!group) { await el.dispose(); continue; }
375: 
376:           const read = () => el.evaluate((e, { P, PA }) => {
377:             const pack = (ps, props) => {
378:               const c = getComputedStyle(e, ps);
379:               return props.map((k) => c[k]).join('|');
380:             };
381:             return pack(null, P) + ' || ' + pack('::after', PA);
382:           }, { P: PROPS, PA: PROPS_AFTER });
383: 
384:           const box = await el.boundingBox();
385:           if (!box) { await el.dispose(); continue; }
386:           const cx = box.x + box.width / 2;
387:           const cy = box.y + box.height / 2;
388: 
389:           // hover first, then active, then focus-visible
390:           await page.mouse.move(cx, cy);
391:           await page.waitForTimeout(600);
392:           const hover = await read();
393: 
394:           await page.mouse.down();
395:           await page.waitForTimeout(700);
396:           const active = await read();
397:           await page.mouse.up();
398:           await page.mouse.move(0, 0);
399:           await page.waitForTimeout(150);
400: 
401:           await el.focus();
402:           await page.keyboard.press('Shift');
403:           await page.waitForTimeout(600);
404:           const focus = await read();
405:           await el.evaluate((e) => e.blur());
406:           await el.dispose();
407: 
408:           totalButtons++;
409:           measurements.push({
410:             page: pagePath,
411:             group,
412:             classAttr: meta.classAttr,
413:             text: meta.text,
414:             hover, focus, active,
415:           });
416:         }
417:       } finally {
418:         await page.close().catch(() => {});
419:       }
420:     }
421:   } finally {

433:     g.n++;
434:     for (const state of STATES) {
435:       const map = g.sigs[state];
436:       if (!map.has(m[state])) map.set(m[state], []);
437:       map.get(m[state]).push(m);
438:     }
439:   }

441:   for (const [group, g] of byGroup) {
442:     const counts = STATES.map((s) => g.sigs[s].size);
443:     console.log(`${group}: ${g.n} buttons, hover/focus/active distinct signatures = ${counts.join('/')}`);

445:       const map = g.sigs[state];
446:       if (map.size > 1) {
447:         fail(`${group} ${state}: ${map.size} different looks`);
448:         for (const [, items] of map) {
449:           for (const it of items.slice(0, 2)) {
450:             console.log(`  e.g. ${it.page} class="${it.classAttr}" text="${it.text}" sig=${it[state].slice(0, 200)}`);
451:           }
452:         }
453:       }
454:     }
455:   }

460: // ---------------------------------------------------------------- API
461: 
462: async function checkInteractionContract(argv = []) {
463:   const failures = staticChecks();
464:   let buttons = 0;
465:   let pages = 0;
466:   if (!argv.includes('--static-only')) {
467:     const dyn = await dynamicChecks(failures);
468:     buttons = dyn.buttons;
469:     pages = dyn.pages;

1: # Component registry
2: 
3: The reuse engine. **Check here before harvesting anything.** If a page needs a
4: component that already exists, compose it and skip the Figma → UI kit → pattern
5: library round trip entirely.
6: 
7: ## Layout
8: 
9: ```text
10: components/<component-name>/
11: ├── README.md        # required: what it is, where it came from, how to install it
12: ├── *.html           # verbatim markup fragment(s) when harvested from markup
13: ├── *.css            # only if the component carries its own styles
14: ├── manifest.json    # required: source, fragments, css/js, assets, figma pointer
15: ├── verify.json      # required: section spec (counts, taps, expectCss/hoverCss/pressCss)
16: ├── figma/           # only if the component is Figma-editable (see below)
17: │   ├── spec.json    # paste source: root key, instances, props, geometry, overrides
18: │   ├── copy.json    # moved copy/icons/props (Figma is boss for copy)
19: │   ├── build.js     # one-shot rebuild (must reproduce the frame with no hand-patches)
20: │   ├── evidence/    # committed verification screenshots (final frames only)
21: │   └── README.md    # per-component edit notes (paste/edit/replace commands)

240:   *composed* into pages. One Figma section = one component.
241: - **Element** — a nested part *inside* a component (hero eyebrow, portal table,
242:   a card). Elements live and are verified with their parent component; they are
243:   NOT separately registered.
244: - **Promote element → component only on second use.** If an element is needed
245:   by another page/section, extract it then — not before. (HB05's portal mock
246:   stays an element until something else needs it.)

250:   SVG-flatten them (`skills/figma-uikit-to-design`).

257:

259:    README), then composed into the page. The page is the last step, not the first.

261:    fallback is required (see `skills/clone-web-element`).
262: 3. Figma update to an existing page: if every section maps to a registered
263:    component, edit the prototype HTML directly.
264: 4. Keep component folders dependency-free — no imports from other components
265:    unless the README says so, so a page can include just what it needs.
266: 5. Figma edits go through `figma/spec.json`, never bare `use_figma` one-offs:
267:    export → record `overrides` → paste to scratch → screenshot-verify →
268:    replace on the page (`skills/figma-component-edit`). Commit the updated
269:    spec with the change so the next agent pastes the edited version.
270: 6. After every fold into a one-shot Figma builder, re-prove it fresh and
271:    screenshot-compare before swapping; re-save the Figma baseline only for
272:    a verified intended change (never to silence a diff) and re-point all
273:    stored node ids. Rules of engagement: `skills/figma-component-edit` §4.
274: 7. Shared tree: rebase, never force-push; re-run the sync gate after every
275:    pull; stage only your own files (a parallel session works here).

# Component registry

The reuse engine. **Check here before harvesting anything.** If a page needs a
component that already exists, compose it and skip the Figma → UI kit → pattern
library round trip entirely.

## Layout

```text
components/<component-name>/
├── README.md        # required: what it is, where it came from, how to install it
├── *.html           # verbatim markup fragment(s) when harvested from markup
├── *.css            # only if the component carries its own styles
├── manifest.json    # required: source, fragments, css/js, assets, figma pointer
├── verify.json      # required: section spec (counts, taps, expectCss/hoverCss/pressCss)
├── figma/           # only if the component is Figma-editable (see below)
│   ├── spec.json    # paste source: root key, instances, props, geometry, overrides
│   ├── copy.json    # moved copy/icons/props (Figma is boss for copy)
│   ├── build.js     # one-shot rebuild (must reproduce the frame with no hand-patches)
│   ├── evidence/    # committed verification screenshots (final frames only)
│   └── README.md    # per-component edit notes (paste/edit/replace commands)
└── assets/ or *.svg # images/icons the fragment references
```

`figma/` holds the Figma-editable counterpart: `spec.json` lets any agent
paste the component as a live instance with correct properties, edit those
properties, and replace a page instance — no cross-file copy/paste needed
(Plugin API has none). Workflow: `skills/figma-component-edit` +
`tooling/figma-export.js` / `figma-paste.js` / `figma-replace.js`. Every script that
sends code to Figma goes through **`tooling/figma-run.js`** (CLI + `callFigma(code,
fileKey, desc)`): one payload transport, one place where proxy noise is filtered and a
`Error:` line decides the exit code. Section builders live in the project
(`ongoing_project/<project>/figma/<section>/build.js`) and assert their own output —
see `ongoing_project/sage50accountant/figma/README.md`.
`play-overlay` is the pilot; add `figma/` to a component when its Figma
properties first need editing — not upfront. Cross-cutting references:
`docs/kit-variables.md` (all 478 kit variables with per-breakpoint values —
grep here before any Figma variable scan), `skills/build-instruction`
(instruction + term registry rules mirror these mechanics).

`site-header` carries **`navigation/`** instead of `figma/`. The nav is not a page
section — there is no pattern to paste — so its Figma side is a config-driven kit:
one JSON per market drives a builder that writes GN01 + SN01 into any design file as
live library instances, plus a gate that asserts the same config against the live
page DOM. Start at `site-header/navigation/README.md`; the CA worked example is
`ongoing_project/sage50accountant/figma/nav/` (its `build.js`/`verify-nav.js` are
wrappers over the kit, so there is one implementation to fix).

## Term registry (`figma/terms.json`, schema v1) + builder token lint

No component composes without a term registry: `source` (instruction frame,
pattern demo, Figma section, site), `breakpoints` ([390,768,1440,1920]),
`terms[]` (rendering/layout: `term`, `cmsIdPrefix`, `site` class, `figma`
counterpart, `status`), `params[]` (sized values: `term`, `token` as
authored, `kitVar` {name, values} | bound-string | NONE, `figma` value,
`siteBreakpoints`[4], `status`, `verify`, `note`), `autoWrappers[]`
(renderings in saves but not instructions, mechanism + pending proof),
`nameMismatches[]`, `openQuestions[]`. Status enum: `match`,
`match-responsive`, `match-geometric`, `match-large/responsive-mid`,
`GAP-*`. Reference: `pn02-highlights-6col/figma/terms.json`.

`tooling/check-builder-tokens.js` is the authorship gate: every number a
`figma/build.js` payload writes must be a named const, a copy.json/spec
value, or a `// token-allow: <num> <reason>` entry (derivations marked
`Phase 4: compute`). Clean exit 0 required pre-commit (AGENTS.md gates).

## New-component variable integration (instruction → Figma → Vercel)

Every new component ships this chain, in order — none of it optional:

1. **Instruction first:** write the Sitecore tree + option tokens
   (`skills/build-instruction` §1), one term per rendering.
2. **Registry:** `figma/terms.json` (schema v1 above) with `options[]` on
   every option-family param (all legal tokens + site classes + Figma
   values + proof) and `bindings[]` for every live binding, prop, and
   style link.
3. **Figma build:** masters by key, layout frames (never bare FIXED),
   variables BOUND not written (`setBoundVariable` after import-by-KEY),
   text styles ASSIGNED by key on exact size match (sole genuine override
   kept), slots/props pinned — then `check-bindings.js` 100% green.
   **Rhythm included: the spacing is a bound FIELD (the frame's own
   `paddingTop`/`paddingBottom`, a `paddingBottom` on the heading stylebox,
   a bound `itemSpacing` per gap), never a `spacer` frame and never an
   absolute y.** A filler frame is a number nobody owns and carries one
   fixed value; a bound field carries the `Breakpoints` mode (40 at Mobile,
   80 at Large desktop) and cannot drift. Assert the token name as well as
   the resolved value (`boundName(node, 'paddingTop')` — a raw 80 and a
   bound 80 read back identically) and assert that no filler frame survives.
   How the same pattern is built in the reference file (`XO7YuDahwIZ1WCq8IoQ6Mo`)
   is the construction to copy; see `skills/figma-section-replace` and
   `figma/README.md` rule 6 for the CA HB05/TS03 numbers.
4. **Site compose:** pattern demo verbatim, option classes only (triple
   proof: variant + bundle + CMS saves), zero custom values.
5. **Sync proof:** `translate-variables.js --comp` clean both... dry-clean
   Figma→site AND a reverse report that shows the way back; write paths
   proven on a throwaway fixture, never on live files.
6. **Gates:** token lint + bindings + sync-check green before commit.

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| `source:` | `atomic-ui` \| `pattern-library` \| `custom` — atomic-ui wins (roadmap 1.5) |
| Source URL / snippet path | re-harvest without re-discovering |
| Harvested date + version/pin | detect drift |
| Install snippet | copy-paste into a page |
| Fallbacks / known gaps | JS-driven states, library drift, no-JS notes |
| Used in | which pages depend on it (grep this before changing it) |

## Terminology (binding)

- **Pattern** — a named Sitecore design (`HB05`, `PN11`): has a snippet path
  and a pattern-library page. Patterns are *harvested*, never invented.
- **Component** — a built, registered unit under `components/<name>/`
  (fragment + fallback CSS/JS + assets + README + manifest). Components are
  *composed* into pages. One Figma section = one component.
- **Element** — a nested part *inside* a component (hero eyebrow, portal table,
  a card). Elements live and are verified with their parent component; they are
  NOT separately registered.
- **Promote element → component only on second use.** If an element is needed
  by another page/section, extract it then — not before. (HB05's portal mock
  stays an element until something else needs it.)
- **Instance / Variant (Figma)** — an instance is a usage of a library
  component; a variant is a prop-driven version (`style: single cta`,
  `Colour: over dark`). Rebuilds preserve instances via import-by-key, never
  SVG-flatten them (`skills/figma-uikit-to-design`).
- **Figma spec** — `components/<name>/figma/spec.json`: the paste source for
  a component's live Figma instance (root key, nested instances, props,
  geometry, `overrides`). Edits are recorded as `overrides` so every agent
  and every future paste gets them (`skills/figma-component-edit`).

## Rules

1. A component built for a page is saved here **first** (markup + assets +
   README), then composed into the page. The page is the last step, not the first.
2. Copy, never hand-rewrite, harvested markup — rewrite only where a documented
   fallback is required (see `skills/clone-web-element`).
3. Figma update to an existing page: if every section maps to a registered
   component, edit the prototype HTML directly.
4. Keep component folders dependency-free — no imports from other components
   unless the README says so, so a page can include just what it needs.
5. Figma edits go through `figma/spec.json`, never bare `use_figma` one-offs:
   export → record `overrides` → paste to scratch → screenshot-verify →
   replace on the page (`skills/figma-component-edit`). Commit the updated
   spec with the change so the next agent pastes the edited version.
6. After every fold into a one-shot Figma builder, re-prove it fresh and
   screenshot-compare before swapping; re-save the Figma baseline only for
   a verified intended change (never to silence a diff) and re-point all
   stored node ids. Rules of engagement: `skills/figma-component-edit` §4.
7. Shared tree: rebase, never force-push; re-run the sync gate after every
   pull; stage only your own files (a parallel session works here).
